answer: Tundra River Yarrow Watch: each identity owns one $10 temperature probe buried in tundra soil, in a yarrow stand on a named Arctic riverbank, logging soil temperature hourly to a public log. A fake needs its own probe in the ground for a full winter, because each log carries one probe serial and one site, so probes cannot be shared. The thaw auditor rejects any log whose thaw date misses the river's published ice-breakup by a day, and checks the yarrow's first-bloom photo against the same date; a fabricated curve fails the breakup date, and a copied log is caught by duplicate serials.
